item.title: Speculative Application
item.description: The European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR) is an award-winning international think-tank that aims to conduct cutting-edge independent research on European foreign and security policy and to provide a safe meeting space for decision-makers, activists and influencers to share ideas. We build coalitions for change at the European level and promote informed debate about Europe’s role in the world. In 2007, ECFR’s founders set about creating a pan-European institution that could combine establishment credibility with intellectual insurgency. Today, ECFR remains uniquely placed to continue providing a pan-European perspective on some of the biggest strategic challenges and choices Europeans need to confront, with a network of offices in seven European capitals, over 90 staff from more than 25 different countries and a team of associated researchers in the EU 27 member states. For more information check our website: ecfr.eu

item.title: PPCA Secretariat Coordinator, London
item.description: PPCA Secretariat Coordinator, Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA), London This London-based role will support delivery of the PPCA Secretariat by coordinating events, steering committee and member engagement, and internal processes ensuring smooth day-to-day operations across the PPCA. Background The Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) is a coalition of over 180 members working to advance the transition from unabated coal power generation to clean energy. Founded in 2017 by the United Kingdom and Canada its membership now includes almost a third of the world’s countries, financial institutions, sub-national governments in the most coal-dependent regions in the world and leading utilities. The PPCA Secretariat is hosted by E3G, an independent climate change think tank, which provides management and administrative support to the Secretariat, plus strategic analysis and advice. E3G is the world lead strategist think tank on the political economy of climate change with a global outlook. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate for all. We translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. We pride ourselves on bringing independence to an extremely polarised discussion and holding policy makers to account on their promises. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top-ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. E3G is dedicated to fostering an engaging work environment with a competitive remuneration package in the non-profit sector. E3G offers a dynamic and fast paced working environment that will value your insight and initiative wherever you are in the organisation. We take pride in our team's commitment, supportiveness, and friendliness. We invest in our staff, offer flexible working conditions and pride ourselves on being an open and collaborative workplace. Role Overview The PPCA Secretariat Coordinator plays a central role in supporting the effective delivery of the Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) Secretariat’s work. The role coordinates events, member engagement, governance meetings and operational processes, ensuring smooth collaboration across a global network of governments, businesses and civil society partners. Working closely with the Secretariat Manager, Head of Secretariat and wider E3G teams, the Coordinator provides high-quality logistical, administrative and stakeholder support that enables the PPCA to advance its international mission and deliver impact across a fast-paced and dynamic policy environment. Key Responsibilities Lead preparation for key events Coordinate logistical preparation and delivery of PPCA events, including agendas, timelines, invitations and supporting materials. Manage event logistics such as venue liaison, travel arrangements and scheduling. Maintain and update the PPCA contact database, calendar and forward plan of key meetings and milestones. Conduct background research to support preparation of meetings, briefings and deliverables. Organise meetings and delegations with senior stakeholders Support coordination of meetings and delegations involving senior political, civil society and media stakeholders. Manage logistics including scheduling, travel coordination, agendas and briefing materials. Support the Head of Secretariat with meeting scheduling. Membership coordination Coordinate communication and engagement with PPCA members. Organise PPCA governance and member meetings, including PPCA Steering Committee, Implementation Committee and Members Meetings. Maintain accurate records of member contacts, engagement and correspondence. Work with the communications team and Secretariat Manager to coordinate progress updates on PPCA work. Operations and Internal Coordination Support the development of effective ways of working and communication for a growing Secretariat team based across multiple time zones. Support recruitment processes, including coordinating applications, interviews and candidate correspondence. Strengthen cross-team coordination by contributing to the development and maintenance of internal tools and processes that support events and Secretariat activities. Support drafting of internal documents, reports and correspondence as required. Provide updates on PPCA activities to E3G internal communications, ensuring PPCA updates are shared at staff forums and newsletters. Provide flexible administrative and coordination support to the Secretariat Manager as required. About You Motivated by E3G’s mission and keen to gain hands-on experience in policy-oriented research and stakeholder engagement in an international setting. Several years’ relevant professional experience and track record in a relevant setting. High level of initiative and be positive, organised, resilient, and able to deliver high-quality work on time. Skills & Experience Experience of events management. Experience of building relationships and networks, and working with partner organisations, coalitions, and networks including senior stakeholders. Experience of project and budget management. Prince 2 or other project management training or qualification would be considered relevant but not essential. Very strong written communication skills and advanced written and spoken English. What We Offer Permanent, full-time position. Work-life balance. Enjoy a 35-hour workweek with a hybrid work model and flexitime. 25 vacation days + additional leave between Christmas and New Year. Pension contribution plan E3G offers a reward and benefits package which compares well with other organisations within our sector. The indicative salary range in the UK for this position is between £41,498 - £44,000, dependent on experience and qualifications of the chosen candidate. Yearly process for remuneration review. E3G will require candidates to demonstrate that they have the right to live and work in the jurisdiction in which E3G employs them. Occasional international travel may be required from time to time. We are unable to provide any relocation assistance to candidates who would need to move in order to take up this position. Your Application Please email your application in English and include: A CV of maximum two pages A cover letter of maximum one page outlining why you are applying for this role and when you would be able to start. Recruitment Process First online interview with HR and Team Members Final interview with HR, Secretariat Manager, Head of the PPCA Secretariat The deadline for applications is July 31, 2026. Whilst we very much appreciate the time you will have taken with your application, unfortunately due to the level of response we receive we will not be able to reply to every candidate. Therefore, if you have not heard from us within 2 weeks of the closing date, please assume that on this occasion you have been unsuccessful. E3G values diversity and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. We aim to build an inclusive workforce that is reflective of the populations we support, and actively seek applications from those who are marginalized and underrepresented. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities.

item.title: Senior Communications Officer
item.description: Senior Communications Officer, PPCA, Singapore This post based in Singapore, to lead the PPCA’s communications work to enhance the public debate on the benefits and feasibility of the coal-to-clean transition in Southeast Asia and contribute to PPCA’s wider comms activities, reporting to the Communications Lead. Who We Are The Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) is a coalition of over 180 members working to advance the transition from unabated coal power generation to clean energy. Founded in 2017 by the United Kingdom and Canada its membership now includes almost a third of the world’s countries, financial institutions, sub-national governments in the most coal-dependent regions in the world and leading utilities. The PPCA Secretariat is hosted by E3G, an independent climate change think tank, which provides management and administrative support to the Secretariat, plus strategic analysis and advice. E3G is the world lead strategist think tank on the political economy of climate change with a global outlook. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate for all. We translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. We pride ourselves on bringing independence to an extremely polarised discussion and holding policy makers to account on their promises. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top-ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. E3G is dedicated to fostering an engaging work environment with a competitive remuneration package in the non-profit sector. E3G offers a dynamic and fast paced working environment that will value your insight and initiative wherever you are in the organisation. We take pride in our team's commitment, supportiveness, and friendliness. We invest in our staff, offer flexible working conditions and pride ourselves on being an open and collaborative workplace. Role Overview Lead the PPCA’s communications work to enhance the public debate on the benefits and feasibility of the coal-to-clean transition in Southeast Asia and contribute to PPCA’s wider comms activities, reporting to the Communications Lead. Key Responsibilities Communication Strategy : Work with the PPCA Comms Team, the broader PPCA team, and with relevant governments (PPCA co-chairs: the UK and Canada; CTC co-chairs: France and Indonesia) to lead, develop and deliver comprehensive communication strategies that effectively communicate PPCA’s value proposition to our key target audience, closely following the political and media debates in Southeast Asia to identify where strategic communications can be usefully deployed in order to speed up the coal-to-clean transition. Messaging : Develop and refine compelling and impactful narratives that effectively address local priorities, concerns, and opportunities while creating a compelling vision of a prosperous, resilient future powered by clean energy. Identify regional proof-points and case studies, as well as leverage closed-door PPCA engagements to generate exclusive insights. Operationalise narratives with a wide range of communications material (e.g., press releases, press briefings, social media content, op-eds, blogs, communication support during events), ensuring consistency across all communication channels. Media Relations : Bring a strong understanding of the media landscape in Southeast Asia to the PPCA Team. Cultivate strategic media partnerships through consistent engagement, positioning PPCA and its spokespeople as a valued resource for regional energy transition insights. Proactively identify opportunities to engage the media and pitch stories, deliver media assets, develop speaking points and other supportive material for interviews. Stakeholder Engagement and Events : Establish new partnerships and leverage existing ones to refine and amplify messages and identify and elevate local influential voices in comms activities. Use social media to increase visibility and create and strengthen connections. Coordinate online or in-person events for the PPCA Team, co-creating the initial concept and seeing them through to completion. Support the PPCA team in representing the organisation at other relevant events to establish relationships and enhance the Alliance’s profile. Monitoring and Evaluation : Track and analyse the impact of PPCA’s communications efforts in Southeast Asia, including media coverage, social media tracking and stakeholder feedback. Provide regular reports to senior staff and funders on the effectiveness of communication strategies and identify areas for improvement. Contribute to the broader comms activities of the PPCA’s comms team as required. About You A strong track record of building and maintaining impactful media relations in Southeast Asia, including pitching stories and securing media coverage. An enthusiasm to embrace complex, technical topics, and transform them into compelling narratives about the benefits and feasibility of the energy transition. The versatile and adaptable skills necessary to flourish in a fast-paced and wide-ranging work environment and work across time zones. Capability to meet deadlines independently in fast-paced environments. Fluency in written and spoken English, our working language; additional languages are an asset. Skills & Experience At least five years of professional experience in leading external communications, including developing and implementing communication strategies. Proven experience in working in networks with a strong track record of leading on stakeholder management. Demonstrated ability to work with a diverse range of stakeholders, including governments, think tanks and financial institutions. Proven experience in delivering events. Understanding of digital comms tools and platforms, including social media management, website content management systems, and email marketing. What We Offer Permanent, full-time position. Work-life balance. Enjoy a 35-hour workweek with a hybrid work model and flexitime. 25 vacation days + additional leave between Christmas and New Year. Pension contribution plan (can vary according to location). E3G offers a reward and benefits package which compares well with other organisations within our sector. The indicative salary range in the Singapore is $72,000 SGD - $76,800 SGD dependent on experience and qualifications of the chosen candidate. Yearly process for remuneration review. E3G will require candidates to demonstrate that they have the right to live and work in the jurisdiction in which E3G employs them. Occasional international travel may be required from time to time. We are unable to provide any relocation assistance to candidates who would need to move in order to take up this position. Your Application Are you ready to embark on an exhilarating journey where your ambition meets passion? Submit your application in English with a CV of maximum 2 pages and an offer letter of no more than 1 page outlining why you are applying for this role and when you would be able to start. Please combine into a one document submission. Recruitment Process First online interview with HR and Team Members Final online interview with HR, PPCA Communications Lead, and Head of Secretariat The deadline for applications is 31 July 2026. Whilst we very much appreciate the time you will have taken with your application, unfortunately due to the level of response we receive we will not be able to reply to every candidate. Therefore, if you have not heard from us within 2 weeks of the closing date, please assume that on this occasion you have been unsuccessful. item.title: Programme & Events Intern - Paris Office
item.description: The purpose of the internship is two-fold: 1) provide support for event organization, administration, and social media communication of the Paris office and 2) assist in a research project on the challenges of decarbonization, climate action and competitiveness in France, in the context of the 2027 presidential election. The internship will combine desk research on party programs, candidates, intellectual debates on these topics, and, when possible, in-person interviews and participation to conferences. The intern will gain practical experience in a dynamic, multinational environment. Event and Advocacy Support: Assist with the organization and logistics of events and outreach activities for the Paris office, including tracking RSVPs, booking accommodations and transportation, and managing event-related communications. Social Media and CRM Management: Contribute to managing the program’s social media presence, assist with maintaining the CRM system, and support the network engagement and communication efforts. Research Project Support: Assist with research on French debates on climate, decarbonization, and competitiveness in the context of the 2027 presidential election , draft research papers and prepare research briefings. Translation and Administrative Support: Provide general office support, including processing orders for supplies, handling logistics for staff events (e.g., retreats, parties), and assisting with day-to-day administrative tasks. Team Collaboration: Work closely with the Paris coordination team , the DARE team as well as Communications and Advocacy departments and provide flexible support for a variety of tasks, ensuring smooth operations and assisting with urgent needs as they arise. Current university student (Master’s) in Political Science, International Relations, Economics, Social Sciences, or a related discipline. A Convention de stage with your university is required . Strong academic background in political science with a focus on international relations, EU foreign policy, or economics Fluent in French and English Organizational Skills: Well-organized, with the ability to multi-task effectively, prioritize responsibilities, and maintain attention to detail. Proactivity and Flexibility: Proactive, self-motivated, and flexible, able to work both independently and as part of a multinational team. Communication and Interpersonal Skills: Strong communication skills, with ease in drafting invitations, engaging in social interactions, and presenting ideas. Comfortable working in a multicultural environment and able to adapt communication styles accordingly. Technical Proficiency: Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and experienced in using tools like CRM systems , Canva and WordPress. Reliability and Quality Focus: Detail-oriented, reliable, and committed to delivering high-quality work with a positive attitude. Teamwork and Management: Capable of managing tasks efficiently, prioritizing and multitasking in a fast-paced environment, with strong interpersonal and social skills that contribute to team success. Stipend according to local laws and regulations (around 4.50 euros per hour for 35 hours/week) Flexible and hybrid working mode Lunch Voucher Generous leave policy An exciting environment in an innovative, pan-European think-tank An open and appreciative culture within the organization High level of personal responsibility. Committed multicultural and diverse colleagues from across Europe A modern workplace in the heart of Paris Practical experience in a dynamic, multinational environment. If this is of interest, we look forward to receiving your application! Please use the apply button to submit your cover letter and CV (max. 2 pg. and pdf format) Application Deadline: 20th July 2026 Candidates must be eligible to work in France, enrolled as a student, and should be available from mid-September 2026 to mid-March 2027 We aim to keep you posted with the status of your application, but due to high volume of applicants, we are unable to communicate with all applicants individually. If you are not contacted within 2 weeks of closing date, please consider you have not been pre-selected. We care about your data privacy. If you are interested to know more about how we manage your personal data, you can find more information in this link: https://ecfr.eu/privacy-job-applicants/ ECFR is an Equal Opportunity Employer and we do not discriminate against applicants due to race, ethnicity, gender, veteran status, or on the basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class. item.title: Senior Policy Advisor, Trade Diplomacy, Japan
item.description: Senior Policy Advisor, Trade Diplomacy, Japan E3G is looking for a Senior Policy Advisor to lead analysis and engagement on trade diplomacy within its Japan programme. The new role will sit within E3G’s Global Clean Power Diplomacy team and will work closely with our Japan and trade experts to develop E3G’s work on the intersection of Japan’s trade policy, energy and economic security strategies, and climate objectives – with trade playing a key role as a diplomatic lever across these areas contributing to accelerating the clean energy transition. The role The role will build on existing work on trade and its use as a diplomatic lever, leading the development of strategies and engagements to align Japan’s trade, and economic policies, with the goals of a clean energy transition and ambitious climate action. The candidate will be based in Japan and will be required to work remotely. We are looking for an intellectually curious, enthusiastic person with experience of condensing and communicating complex information into clear, targeted analysis and advice for varied stakeholders. You will be motivated by building relationships with external stakeholders, and by creating impactful outcomes through strategic collaborations. You will have the opportunity to develop the strategy and shape the work programme, in consultation with colleagues in the Japan team and across E3G’s wider trade and industry related teams. Background E3G is an independent climate change think tank with a global outlook. We are world leading strategists on the political economy of climate change, dedicated to achieving a safe climate for all. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate. Our goal is to translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. Delivering a rapid, managed transition of the global power system from coal-to-clean, not via gas, is a fundamental condition to achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement. E3G’s Global Clean Power Diplomacy team mobilises diplomatic actors to drive real-world, real-economy progress on ending the global use of the coal power and transitioning to clean energy. E3G identifies opportunities for influence and interventions, collaborates with civil society campaigns and partners, and fosters international diplomatic alliances to create a world where no new coal is built, and where existing coal is replaced by clean, affordable energy to enable a climate-safe world. Key Responsibilities Provide strategic insight and thought leadership on trade and diplomatic engagement with Japan in the context of broader global climate and energy goals. Monitor and track developments relating to Japan’s trade relationships with a focus on key partner countries, including various bilateral and multilateral frameworks and agreements (e.g. FTAs), government strategies and publications (e.g. Green Transformation Strategy; and industrial policy priorities, such as the 17 Strategic Fields under Japan’s growth strategy etc.), as well as commercial drivers relating to both traditional and clean energy supply chains, in order to assess their impact on Japan’s energy and economic security priorities and identify opportunities for strategic interventions. Produce analysis, presentations, briefings and other materials, both internally to contribute to E3Gs strategic thinking, and to a wide range of external contacts to communicate our analysis and recommendations, in both written and spoken formats. Expand E3G’s relationships and networks to relevant institutions and stakeholders in trade, energy and economic security – particularly civil society organisations (CSOs), alongside government officials, research institutions, trade associations and key private sector actors, primarily in Japan and key trade partner countries, to develop productive collaborations that support achieving the programme’s objectives. In collaboration with E3G’s Japan experts and trusted partners, maintain and widen the team’s relationships with diplomats and foreign missions and trade representatives to distribute analysis and strategic advice, for example through organising and presenting in online and in-person briefings. Represent E3G externally through active participation in civil society meetings, as well as relevant conferences and other events in Japan and internationally as needed; and maintain relations to media and provide commentary and insights about their area of expertise when needed. Experience and Skills A graduate degree in a relevant discipline, such as trade policy, international relations, climate and energy policy, development, geography, or politics. A minimum of six years of relevant professional experience in a related field, such as trade, policy, research or advocacy within a government or international organisation, commercial sector, think tank, civil society or research institute. Established connections to organisations and individuals relevant for the role, e.g. government and ministries, trade associations or related research institutions, and the ability to leverage these relationships effectively and in alignment with organisational priorities. Strong analytical and strategic thinking, with an aptitude for learning new areas and consider complex information to make evidence-based recommendations. Excellent communication skills, able to convey information and arguments to others in a clear, accessible and convincing way including in sensitive or challenging stakeholder contexts. Highly organised and attention to detail, able to be proactive and deliver high-quality outputs in a timely manner. Strong interpersonal skills, with ability to form high-trust relationships with various external stakeholders and handle sensitive information with discretion, as well as patience and resilience in long-term engagement processes. Excellent written and spoken Japanese and English. Ability to work effectively and collaboratively in an international team environment. What we offer Initial contract of one year, with possibility of extension, for a full-time position. Fully remote and flexible working arrangements. 16 vacation days + additional leave between Christmas and New Year. Eligible for social (employee health) insurance and employment insurance. E3G offers a competitive salary and reward package which compares well with other organisations within our sector, reflecting experience and qualifications of the chosen candidate. The salary shall be subject to withholdings for taxes and social and labor insurances in Japan mentioned above in which the Senior Policy Advisor will be enrolled. Yearly process for remuneration review. E3G is unable to provide relocation assistance to candidates who would need to change locations in order to take up this position. E3G will require candidates to demonstrate that they the right to live and work in Japan. How to apply Please submit your application in English. Please include: A CV of maximum two pages A cover letter of no more than one page outlining why you are applying for this role and when you would be able to start. Please include a written description of your residency status and right to work in Japan (for example, your visa status, if applicable), in the letter. The deadline for applications is Midnight, Sunday 16th August. Whilst we very much appreciate the time you will have taken with your application, unfortunately due to the level of response we receive we may not be able to reply to every candidate. Therefore, if you have not heard from us with 2 weeks of the closing date, please assume that on this occasion you have been unsuccessful. E3G values diversity and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. We aim to build an inclusive workforce that is reflective of the populations we support, and actively seek applications from those who are marginalized and underrepresented. Role Summary TBI's Digital function exists to enable the Institute's global mission by ensuring our people have the platforms, applications and engineering capability to operate effectively at scale. Following a period of foundational delivery, including the establishment of Cyber Essentials+ certification, a live SOC, Salesforce as our CRM platform, the stabilisation of our Workday investment, and the building of our data warehouse foundations, Digital is moving into a phase focused on platform maturity, AI-enabled operations and engineering excellence. The Director of Applications is a new, senior role accountable for the availability, configuration and ongoing evolution of TBI's core business platforms: Salesforce, Workday, and Microsoft 365 / Azure, together with the engineering practice, AI platform operations and platform-level roadmaps that underpin them. Reporting to the CTO, this role leads the Applications function, owns the platform Centre of Excellence, and provides the technical leadership that translates business needs into delivered platform capability. You will be an experienced applications leader with deep expertise in SaaS platforms, modern engineering practice (CI/CD, source control, environment and release management, test automation) and the operational realities of running mission-critical business systems globally. You will work closely with the CTO, the Head of Digital Transformation & Performance, the Enterprise Architect, the Director of Security & Compliance, and the platform leads to ensure our applications estate enables rather than constrains TBI's ambitions. Key Responsibilities Platform Leadership Accountable for the availability, configuration and ongoing management of TBI's three strategic platforms: Salesforce, Workday, and Microsoft 365 / Azure Own the platform-level roadmaps that enable delivery of the Digital Roadmap, in close collaboration with the Digital Leadership Team and Platform Leads Establish and lead the platform Centre of Excellence; platform-specific standards, delivery patterns and an internal community across the platform leads and developers Line management responsibility for the Build team Engineering Practice Own engineering practice across the Applications function: source control and repository governance (GitHub, Salesforce via Gearset), CI/CD pipelines, environment management (dev/test/UAT/prod parity and access), release management and test strategy / automation Define and enforce technical execution standards for releases, distinct from the change control approval process Define and lead engineering standards, architectural patterns and Infrastructure as Code AI Platform Operations Accountable for the operational availability of TBI's internal AI platforms (Claude, Agentforce, AI assistants) and ongoing AI consumption cost and budget management Own AI usage monitoring: drift, hallucination and misuse pattern detection, partnering with the Director of Security & Compliance, who owns AI security and the Responsible Use Policy Provide the operational foundation that enables TBI's Agentic AI and Generative AI capability pillars Capacity & Observability Own scaling (design and operation), rightsizing and optimisation of cloud and SaaS resources Own application monitoring, alerting and on-call response for in-scope platforms Lead cross-platform test strategy and quality standards Cross-Functional Working Partner with the Digital Leadership to translate business needs (the Digital Roadmap) into platform-level delivery (Platform Roadmaps) Partner with the Director of Security & Compliance on identity, access, secret management and DevSecOps practices embedded in CI/CD Partner with the Enterprise Architect on significant technical decisions and integration patterns Support the CTO with platform investment cases, vendor negotiation for strategic platforms and Executive-level reporting on platform health Person Specification Significant senior leadership experience running enterprise application functions in a mid-to-large global organisation Deep expertise in at least two of: Salesforce, Workday, and Microsoft 365 / Azure or AWS as enterprise platforms (configuration, integration, governance, licensing, support) Demonstrable experience embedding modern engineering practice incl. CI/CD pipelines, source control governance, environment management, release management, automated testing, in a SaaS-heavy environment Track record of building and running Centres of Excellence around major platforms Experience operationalising AI platforms and managing AI consumption cost is a strong advantage Strong understanding of how applications-layer decisions intersect with security, identity, data and architecture, and a collaborative working style with peers in those functions Experience managing technical leads and platform specialists, and a track record of developing them Comfortable operating at executive level on platform investment cases and roadmap trade-offs Pragmatic and delivery-oriented; able to make and defend decisions about where to invest engineering effort Open and progressive; bold and pragmatic; an optimistic changemaker — aligned with TBI's core beliefs Candidates must have the legal right to work in the UK to apply for this role. We reserve the right to close this role early if we receive a sufficient number of applications. Closing Date: 2026-08-09

Role Summary The Tony Blair Institute, in partnership with the Rwanda Development Board, is seeking to recruit an exceptional Advisor – Tourism Competitiveness & Investment Facilitation to support Rwanda’s ambition to strengthen its position as a premium, high-quality, and diversified tourism destination. This role will be embedded within the Rwanda Development Board (RDB) and will work closely with the Tourism Office, regulatory counterparts, investment facilitation teams, and wider government stakeholders. The Advisor will support two mutually reinforcing priorities: first, strengthening hospitality service quality standards, inspection practice, and enforcement credibility; and second, advancing tourism product diversification and improving the investment facilitation systems required to attract, assess, and convert high-quality tourism investments. The position will support RDB to improve the consistency and credibility of hospitality regulation through clearer service quality standards, better inspection operations, and practical enforcement improvements. In parallel, the Advisor will help the Tourism Office identify priority gaps in Rwanda’s tourism offer, build a structured pipeline of diversified tourism product opportunities, assess incoming investor proposals, and strengthen coordination across the tourism investment facilitation process. The role requires a strong delivery-oriented professional who can bridge tourism sector strategy, service quality, regulation, investment facilitation, institutional coordination, and practical implementation. The Advisor will be expected to diagnose operational and market bottlenecks, design practical tools and frameworks, support institutional adoption, and work hands-on with government teams to improve the systems that underpin tourism competitiveness, visitor experience, and investment conversion. This is not a traditional advisory role. It requires someone able to move between policy, operations, investors, and delivery; translate strategic priorities into usable tools and routines; and help RDB build stronger internal capability across both hospitality quality enforcement and tourism product development. Role Responsibilities 1. Strategic Tourism Competitiveness Advisory Advise RDB and the Tourism Office on practical interventions to strengthen Rwanda’s tourism competitiveness, with balanced attention to hospitality service quality, regulatory credibility, tourism product diversification, and investment facilitation Support the translation of Rwanda’s premium tourism positioning and NST2 tourism priorities into clear operational reforms, product opportunities, tools, and delivery plans Provide analysis on service quality gaps, regulatory bottlenecks, tourism product gaps, investor requirements, institutional coordination challenges, and implementation constraints Support RDB leadership to prioritize high-impact actions that improve the visitor experience, strengthen regulatory credibility, diversify Rwanda’s tourism offer, and improve investor confidence Prepare concise briefs, decision papers, product opportunity notes, and implementation updates for senior government and RDB stakeholders 2. Hospitality Service Quality Standards & Regulation Conduct a rapid diagnostic of current hospitality inspection, classification, and enforcement practices to identify key gaps, bottlenecks, and root causes Support the design of a tiered hospitality service quality standards framework covering facilities, service delivery, and staff conduct Develop practical tools that can be used by both hospitality operators and inspectors as a clear compliance reference and objective inspection benchmark Develop an inspection operations guide setting out how inspections should be planned, conducted, documented, escalated, and followed up Identify quick wins and prepare a short-term enforcement improvement roadmap to strengthen inspection consistency, regulatory credibility, and service quality follow-through 3. Tourism Product Diversification & Pipeline Development Support RDB’s Tourism Office to develop a structured tourism product diversification pipeline aligned with NST2 priorities and Rwanda’s premium destination positioning Map Rwanda’s current tourism product offer and identify priority gaps and opportunities across high-value and emerging tourism segments Develop a framework for prioritizing tourism product opportunities based on strategic fit, market demand, investor appetite, feasibility, geographic spread, contribution to length of stay, and alignment with national targets Support the Tourism Office to convert priority product categories into clear opportunity concepts and investor-facing propositions Build and maintain a prioritized pipeline of tourism product opportunities, including new concepts, active investor leads, proposals under assessment, and opportunities requiring cross-government support 4. Tourism Investment Facilitation & Investor Assessment Design a front-end investor assessment framework enabling the Tourism Office to evaluate investor seriousness, strategic fit, and project quality at the earliest stage of engagement Assess incoming tourism investment proposals against agreed criteria, including investor seriousness, product quality, destination fit, commercial viability, sustainability, and potential contribution to Rwanda’s tourism objectives Develop an investor journey and decision-point guide clarifying roles, responsibilities, handover points, and escalation channels across RDB departments and partner agencies Develop and operationalise an investment monitoring tracker to record investor interactions, assessment outcomes, pipeline status, and next steps Support follow-through on priority investor engagements, ensuring that bottlenecks are identified, escalated, and resolved in a timely manner 5. Coordination, Institutional Strengthening & Capacity Building Establish a coordination embedding toolkit, including standardized templates, escalation protocols, and operating procedures for both tourism investment facilitation and quality service follow-through Strengthening coordination between the Tourism Office, investment facilitation teams, regulatory counterparts, and relevant partner agencies Design and deliver capacity-building sessions to equip Tourism Office staff and relevant counterparts to use the service quality tools, investor assessment framework, coordination protocols, and monitoring tracker independently Support regular review routines with RDB teams to track progress, unblock constraints, and maintain delivery discipline across both workstreams Contribute to embedding a more data-driven, results-oriented, service-quality-focused, and investor-responsive culture within the relevant RDB teams Candidate Profile 10+ years of relevant experience in tourism Role Summary About the Geopolitics Team TBI’s Geopolitics Team provides senior political and corporate leaders with distinctive, decision-relevant insight on the geopolitical forces shaping their priorities. The team briefs senior TBI leadership, government principals and C-suite clients, connecting political developments to their second- and third-order implications for strategy, policy, markets, investment, operations and risk. TBI is embedded with governments across the world and is growing its corporate client service footprint. The team therefore needs analysts who are equally comfortable briefing a senior public principal and a corporate executive, and who can translate complex political developments into clear implications for decisions. Role Overview The Senior Analyst will support TBI’s coverage of Asia-Pacific, with a particular focus on China. The successful candidate will bring strong foreign-policy judgement, regional expertise, analytical range and an established network across policy, diplomatic, business and expert communities. We are looking for someone who has the tools, curiosity and network to build informed views quickly across political, economic, security, trade, technology and market issues, and to turn fragmented information into distinctive insight for public and private clients. Key Responsibilities Brief senior TBI leadership, public-sector principals and corporate clients on geopolitical developments across China and the wider Asia Pacific Region, with clear implications for decisions and risk exposure. Produce high-quality intelligence briefings, written analysis, data-led insights and client-ready deliverables on China and APAC. Identify second- and third-order implications of political, security, trade, sanctions, technology, election and foreign-policy developments for governments and businesses. item.title: Director of operations and strategy
item.description: Full time, fixed term contract with probation period. P ower to Prosper is a national community wealth building programme, delivered by the New Economics Foundation (NEF) in partnership with a network of community hubs across the UK. The programme works to build community-owned economic power and challenge racial and economic inequality Power to Prosper is in the process of becoming an independent organisation and is currently being incubated within the New Economics Foundation group. During this incubation period, contracts of employment will be offered on a fixed-term basis through NEF Consulting.’ across all the jobs. Working alongside the Executive Director, you will help design and build almost every aspect of the organisation: governance, finance, people, operations, organisational development and compliance. Equally importantly, you will help shape how those things are done. Role: Director of Operations & Strategy Hours of work: 35hrs per week – Monday to Friday Salary: Starting from £60,000 Location: Hybrid — London/​South East with regular travel to the London Office and Hub locations Contract type: Fixed term contract ending 30th September 2028 How to apply Deadline for applications: 12pm Tuesday 1st September 2026 Interviews: First stage interviews offered online on 7th September 2026 with second stage in-person interviews on 14th September 2026, please ensure availability on both dates. Start date: Must be available to start by November 2026 Please answer the following questions on a separate Word document and submit alongside your CV to recruitment@neweconomics.org This is not a conventional Director of Operations role. Alongside leading operations, you’ll help shape the culture, systems and ways of working of a new organisation. What attracts you to this opportunity, and what experience has best prepared you to build an organisation rather than simply manage one? (250 words) Power to Prosper believes organisations cannot address racial inequity simply through good intentions; they must deliberately design their systems, culture and decision-making differently. Tell us about a time when your understanding of structural racism influenced the way you built or changed an organisational system, policy or way of working. What changed as a result? (250 words) Please also complete the equality and diversity monitoring form. You must be eligible to work in the UK, as we are unable to sponsor visas. Inclusivity at Power to Prosper and NEFC Power to Prosper and NEFC wants to be an inclusive workplace with a diverse body of staff. We don’t want to conform to the traditional think-tank model where people from certain backgrounds are hugely under-represented. We know we have some way to go in this and are therefore genuinely keen to receive applications from Black, Asian and minority ethnic people; women; neurodivergent people; disabled people; people who identify as LGBT+; people with experience of mental health problems; and people who identify as working class or have done so in the past. Accessibility and Equal Opportunity We value all candidates and are committed to equal opportunity. As a Disability Confident employer, we guarantee an interview to all disabled applicants who meet the minimum criteria for the role. If you require any reasonable adjustments to support you during the application process, or would like information in an alternative format, please let us know. We actively promote positive action to advance fairness and tackle underrepresentation within our workforce.
